messages:
meera: Bringing up Mistral-21B on int4 on dedicated cluster. Short tests look fine but at 8k context we see a big summarization quality drop vs fp16 + increased repetition. Anyone else hit longctx regressions after quant?

 dmitri: Did you use rotary freq scaling or the default? Also, did you convert the vocab with the new roundtrip map? Token-id shifts can cause kv-cache misalignment which looks like longctx degradation.

 meera: Quick config snippet I used:
```
model: mistral-21b
quant: int4
calib: perchannel
rotary: { base: 10000, scale: 1.0 }
vocab_map: ./maps/mistral_to_redwood.json
kv_cache: enabled
context: 8192
```
I also ran an fp16 baseline on the same checkpoint and that doesn't show the regression. Logs show a small q/k dot mismatch during warmup on the first two layers.

 alex: Can you dump a tiny trace of qk dot diffs for layer 0/1 (first 256 tokens) and paste headwise max/min? Also try setting `rotary.scale=0.5` as a quick experiment — we've previously seen headwise rotary leakage with some int4 kernels.

 meera: Pasted eval summary from eval-bot: `eval-bot: 7881122333 | model=mistral-21b:int4 | dataset=cnn_dailymail | rouge1=0.32 (fp16=0.44) | repetition_score=0.27 (fp16=0.06)` — huge delta.

 dmitri: Yikes. Next quick steps: 1) run `--rotary-scale 0.5` + `--no-autocast` to rule out mixed-precision runtime effects; 2) run vocab roundtrip check: `python tools/verify_vocab_roundtrip.py --map ./maps/mistral_to_redwood.json` to make sure token ids are stable; 3) collect qk diffs: `python tools/dump_qk_diff.py --layer 0,1 --tokens 256 --out /tmp/qk.diff`

 meera: Doing the runs now, will post diffs & results. Thanks :pray:
